narr: Tropical Depression Nine developed in the eastern Caribbean in the morning of Friday, September 23rd. The system steadily strengthened as it tracked to the northeast and became Hurricane Ian in the morning of Monday, September 26th. After making landfall and moving across western Cuba, Ian emerged into the eastern Gulf of Mexico and strengthened into a major hurricane. Ian then made landfall along the southwest Florida coast on Wednesday, September 28th and tracked northeastward across the Florida peninsula. Ian moved into the far western Atlantic as a tropical storm, but quickly strengthened back to a hurricane. Ian then made landfall as a category 1 hurricane near Georgetown, SC at 2:05 pm on Friday, September 30th. Ian brought a myriad of impacts to southeast South Carolina including strong winds, intense rainfall, flash flooding, and some coastal flooding. The heaviest rainfall occurred across the Charleston Tri-County region, with 5-10 inches of rain measured from around Summerville, to North Charleston, to the West Ashley area, downtown Charleston, and James Island. Several instances of flash flooding occurred where the highest rainfall amounts occurred. While the strongest winds occurred along the immediate coastline, widespread tropical storm force wind gusts occurred well inland and produced scattered reports of trees down with some of those down on houses and vehicles.
ev: A NWS employee reported water entering the first floor of a home at 105 Flicker Lane.
North Charleston Fire Department reported that flood waters enter into buildings at the Greenwood at Ashley River Apartment Homes complex.

Local broadcast media reported that flood waters entered several homes on Shoreham Road. Also, a video shared via Twitter showed flood waters entering a detached garage structure at a home located at 1149 Landsdowne Drive. Flooding at both locations was due to heavy rainfall associated with Hurricane Ian.
Video shared via Twitter showed deep water in the ground floor of a house at the corner of Line Street and President Street in downtown Charleston.
Water was reported entering the building at Blessed Sacrament Catholic School on Highway 17 in West Ashley. Flood waters were surrounding the entire school.

Video shared via Twitter shows flood waters entering an attached garage of a home at 4169 Club Course Drive. The home backs up to a small creek that overflowed due to heavy rainfall associated with Hurricane Ian.
